nodes.name: Called by Workflow
nodes.notes: inputSource:passthrough, matching every other callable workflow here. It was `workflowInputs:{values:[]}` — an EMPTY declared schema — and n8n refused to run the workflow at all with WorkflowHasIssuesError. Same trap as a declared schema dropping fields in transit: if you name the inputs, you get only the inputs you named.

parameters.query:
-- Only a lead Instantly ACTUALLY created advances the lifecycle. Reporting a send that did
-- not happen is worse than reporting nothing.
--
-- This is an UPDATE, never an upsert: by the time a lead reaches the sender it already exists, and
-- an insert here would mean the sender inventing a person nobody verified.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
update leads l set
  channel_state_email = 'enrolled',
  sendr_page_url = coalesce(nullif(p.j->>'sendr_page_url', ''), l.sendr_page_url),
  opener         = coalesce(nullif(p.j->>'opener', ''), l.opener),
  updated_at     = now()
from p
where vio_canon(l.contact_email::text) = vio_canon(p.j->>'contact_email')
returning l.id, l.contact_email, l.channel_state_email

-- The outcome. `enrolled` is the word the schema, the daily_stats view and the console all
-- use; the sheet said `enroll`. Writing the sheet's word here would leave the console reporting
-- zero sends and the daily cap counting zero against itself.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
insert into events (lead_id, lead_email, actor, action, outcome, workflow, units, est_cost_usd, payload)
select (select id from leads where vio_canon(contact_email::text) = vio_canon(p.j->>'lead_email')),
       coalesce(p.j->>'lead_email', ''),
       'instantly',
       case when (p.j->>'enrolled')::boolean then 'enrolled' else 'enroll_noop' end,
       coalesce(p.j->>'result', ''),
       'VIO-enrol-email',
       (p.j->>'units')::numeric,
       null,
       jsonb_build_object('instantly_lead_id', p.j->>'instantly_lead_id',
                          'product', p.j->>'source_config')
from p
returning id

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_email: $json.lead_email || '', enrolled: $json.action === 'enroll', units: $json.units, result: $json.result || '', instantly_lead_id: $json.lead_id || '', source_config: $json.source_config || '' }) }}

parameters.query:
-- The write-ahead record: we are ABOUT to POST to Instantly.
--
-- Written before the send, on purpose. If the process dies between this row and the outcome row,
-- the next run sees more attempts than outcomes for that address and REFUSES it — because at that
-- point nobody knows whether the person was contacted, and guessing wrong means mailing a stranger
-- twice.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
insert into events (lead_id, lead_email, actor, action, outcome, workflow, units, est_cost_usd, payload)
select (select id from leads where vio_canon(contact_email::text) = vio_canon(p.j->>'lead_email')),
       coalesce(p.j->>'lead_email', ''),
       'instantly', 'enroll_attempt',
       coalesce(p.j->>'result', ''),
       'VIO-enrol-email', 1, null,
       jsonb_build_object('product', p.j->>'source_config')
from p
returning id

-- Everything the send gate needs, in one question.
--
-- This replaces two whole-tab reads AND the second implementation of suppression matching. That
-- second copy is the reason `test-suppression-parity.mjs` existed: the same canonicalisation lived
-- once in JavaScript here and once in SQL, and a one-case divergence is a person who opted out and
-- gets mailed anyway. There is one implementation now.
--
-- THE DAILY CAP COUNTS `enroll_attempt` AS WELL AS `enrolled`, deliberately. A send whose outcome
-- was never recorded still went out; a cap that only counts confirmed outcomes silently rises every
-- time a run dies between the POST and the write.
--
-- It filters on ACTION ONLY, not on actor. The console's "sent today" and the daily_stats view both
-- count `action = 'enrolled'` with no actor filter, and the number a person reads must be the same
-- number the gate enforces — otherwise the dashboard says 3 while the cap thinks 7.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j),
em as (
  select distinct lower(btrim(e)) as email
  from p, jsonb_array_elements_text(coalesce(p.j->'emails', '[]'::jsonb)) e
  where btrim(e) <> ''
),
cap as (
  -- The cap lives on the campaign, so it can be changed in one place a person can see. 20 only if
  -- the row says nothing.
  select coalesce(max(c.daily_cap), 20) as daily_cap
  from campaigns c, p
  where c.product::text = lower(p.j->>'product')
),
sent as (
  -- THE SENDING TEAM'S DAY, NOT UTC. The UTC day rolls over about five hours before Detroit's, so
  -- counting in UTC would let a send made this evening fall into tomorrow's allowance — up to a
  -- whole extra day's mail inside one real day. The JavaScript this replaces was explicit about
  -- this and the first cut of the port quietly dropped it; the suite caught it.
  select count(*)::int as n from events
   where action in ('enrolled', 'enroll_attempt')
     and at >= date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'America/Detroit') at time zone 'America/Detroit'
)
select
  (select daily_cap from cap)  as daily_cap,
  (select n from sent)         as sent_today,
  coalesce((
    select jsonb_object_agg(e.email, jsonb_build_object(
      -- Every identifier, canonicalised, one implementation.
      'suppressed', is_suppressed(e.email, split_part(e.email, '@', 2), null, null),
      -- The write-ahead reconciliation: more attempts than outcomes means an earlier run died
      -- between the POST and the record, and NOBODY KNOWS whether that person was contacted.
      'started',  (select count(*)::int from events v
                    where lower(v.lead_email::text) = e.email and v.action = 'enroll_attempt'),
      'finished', (select count(*)::int from events v
                    where lower(v.lead_email::text) = e.email
                      and v.action in ('enrolled', 'enroll_noop'))
    ))
    from em e
  ), '{}'::jsonb) as per_email
